$comment: Explore mode (explore.html): one entry per playable zone. Each zone plays one practice scenario (sceneId → CC.scenarios) on a Tiled map (map → assets/game/maps/<map>.tmj, built to .js by tools/build-maps.js). objectives: the compass targets in suggested order; target = a 'target' point on the map; stepId = the scenario step that completes it. encounters: per scenario step, the map zone that starts it, who speaks, and consequences for choices that do not fit (type seeGuide or needInfo): what happens on screen before the player chooses again. Consequences are short fictional reactions; any rule they mention must already be in the choice's claims. facts: things the player unlocks by inspecting objects, talking to people or finishing a moment; every fact rests on claims (CC.claims) and may open a story.

exploreZones.title: A family homestay
exploreZones.intro: You have just arrived at a small family homestay in a Hà Nội street. Your host is waiting at the door; her family is inside, and dinner is nearly ready.

objectives.text: Meet your host at the door
Go in and greet the family

b.speaker: Cô Lan
b.line: She smiles, a little surprised: “Cứ gọi cô là cô Lan nhé — please call me cô Lan.”

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: You step towards the door in your shoes. Cô Lan quickly points at the row of shoes outside.

thenGo.speaker: Cô Lan
thenGo.line: “Mời vào! Come in.” You leave your shoes on the rack and follow her inside.

b.speaker: What happens
b.line: The son looks a little awkward and glances at his grandmother.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: The grandmother nods politely. Cô Lan quietly introduces her mother to you first.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: The grandmother takes the plate. Cô Lan smiles and shows you, with both hands, how she passes dishes.

sc02:s1.notYet: “Dinner is almost ready! Come and say hello to my mother first.”

c.speaker: Cô Lan
c.line: She looks worried: “Không ngon à? Is it not good?”

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: Everyone pauses with their glasses raised, looking at you.

facts.title: Call her what she calls herself
facts.text: Your host introduces herself as “cô”, a family word, not by her name. Use the same word when you speak to her.

facts.title: Take your shoes off at the door
facts.text: Leave your shoes just outside the door of a home. A row of shoes there is your cue.

facts.title: Greet the eldest first
facts.text: Visitors usually greet the oldest people in the family first.

facts.title: Take from shared dishes into your bowl
facts.text: Dishes sit in the middle for everyone. Take food from them into your own small rice bowl.

facts.title: Don’t stand chopsticks in the rice
facts.text: When you pause, rest them across your bowl or on the table.

facts.title: Raise your glass with everyone
facts.text: Glasses are often raised together during the meal.

exploreZones.title: Old Quarter to Hoàn Kiếm Lake
exploreZones.intro: You are walking from your homestay towards Hoàn Kiếm Lake. The street is full of motorbikes, small shops and people selling things on foot.

objectives.text: Ask the way to the lake
Cross the big road to the lake

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: She looks up, a little unsure, and doesn’t answer at first.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: A rider has to brake and swerve to miss you, and honks.

b.speaker: What happens
b.line: Motorbikes swerve around you and someone honks. You get across, but this isn’t a crossing.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: You start to run. A rider brakes hard and honks: running makes you hard to predict.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: She notices, frowns and turns away, pulling her hat down over her face.

facts.title: Call people with “ơi”
facts.text: To ask someone something, use the word that fits their age, then “ơi”. Don’t point or say “excuse me”.

facts.title: Walk at a steady pace
facts.text: Motorbikes may pass close. Riders can predict a steady walker more easily than someone who rushes.

facts.title: Cross at lights, and keep watching
facts.text: Lights and marked crossings are where the law expects you to cross. Keep looking anyway: road rules are often not followed.

facts.title: Keep your bag away from the traffic
facts.text: Carry it in front of you or on the side away from the road.

facts.title: Ask before a photo
facts.text: Ask before you photograph someone. If they say no, accept it calmly.

facts.title: Lake of the Returned Sword
facts.text: Hoàn Kiếm means “Lake of the Returned Sword”. In the legend, Emperor Lê Lợi gave his sword back to a golden turtle here in 1428.

facts.title: The Pen Tower
facts.text: Tháp Bút is a stone tower topped with a writing brush. It carries the words “Tả Thanh Thiên” — writing on the sky. Next to it, three stone frogs hold up an ink slab.

facts.title: Ngọc Sơn Temple
facts.text: The temple on the islet honours General Trần Hưng Đạo and Văn Xương. It was built in 1841 and repaired in 1865 by the scholar Nguyễn Văn Siêu.

facts.title: The Sunbeam Bridge
facts.text: Thê Húc is often called the “Sunbeam Bridge”. The red arched bridge leads across the water to Ngọc Sơn Temple.

exploreZones.title: A street-food stall
exploreZones.intro: It’s lunchtime. A small stall on the pavement is cooking phở and grilling pork for bún chả, and the low plastic stools are filling up.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: Nobody comes. After a while the cook calls over: “Ăn gì? What do you want?”

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: He shrugs and stands waiting with his bowl. The cook looks over, a little puzzled.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: The cook laughs and calls out: “Rau miễn phí! The herbs are free — they come with it.”

sc06:s4.notYet: Your food isn’t ready yet. Find a seat first.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: The cook calls after you and counts the money: it is not quite enough.

facts.title: Order at the front, then sit
facts.text: Point at what you want and ask for “một suất” (one serving). Then find a stool.

facts.title: Expect to share a table
facts.text: At busy times, other diners may sit at your table.

facts.title: Add the herbs as you like
facts.text: Noodle dishes come with a free plate of herbs and greens: mint, coriander, basil, lettuce.

facts.title: Trà đá comes instead of water
facts.text: Iced green tea is served at stalls all over the country.

facts.title: Wipe your chopsticks first
facts.text: A quick wipe of your chopsticks or spoon with a napkin is normal.

facts.title: Eat first, pay on the way out
facts.text: Ask the cook for the total as you leave. Tipping is not expected.

exploreZones.title: Đồng Xuân Market
exploreZones.intro: Hà Nội’s big covered market, on the northern edge of the Old Quarter. Go inside, find something you like, and try shopping the local way.

objectives.text: Go in and find the fabric stall
Look at the clothes stall next door

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: A few people turn round. The seller frowns, unsure who you are calling.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: Her smile disappears and she turns to another customer. People nearby look away, embarrassed.

sc05:s3.notYet: First, see what the fabric seller has.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: The fabric seller shakes her head: you agreed the price. The argument draws a small crowd.

facts.title: A market since 1889
facts.text: Đồng Xuân Market was built in 1889, during the French colonial period, to replace the older Kẻ Chợ markets.

facts.title: Fresh food below, fabric above
facts.text: The ground floor sells fresh food. The upper floors sell fabric, clothes and other goods, often at wholesale prices.

facts.title: Bargain, and keep it friendly
facts.text: Many goods in local markets have no price tag, so bargaining is common. It goes best when you stay polite.

facts.title: Say no and walk on
facts.text: If you don’t want to buy, say “Không, cảm ơn” (No, thank you) and keep walking.

facts.title: Pay the price you agreed
facts.text: Compare a few stalls first. Once you agree a price, it is fair to pay it.

exploreZones.title: Văn Miếu – Quốc Tử Giám
exploreZones.intro: You are visiting the Temple of Literature on a hot morning. Find the gate, the stelae and the worship hall. People still come here to worship, so look around and decide how to act.

c.speaker: Staff member
c.line: Xin lỗi! Excuse me — in the worship areas we ask visitors to dress respectfully.

b.speaker: Staff member
b.line: Please don’t touch the stelae — visitors aren’t allowed to touch them.

c.speaker: What happens
c.line: The woman praying turns away from your camera. A staff member comes over: “Please ask before you photograph people.”

facts.title: Dress respectfully, keep quiet, don’t touch
facts.text: The site’s rules ask for respectful dress in worship areas and quiet in solemn ones. Don’t touch or write on the stelae or artefacts.

facts.title: Ask staff about photos and incense
facts.text: The published rules don’t mention photography or incense. Staff can tell you what is allowed today.

facts.title: Look at the stelae, don’t touch
facts.text: 82 of the original 85 stone stelae survive. Carved between 1484 and 1780, they record the laureates of royal examinations held from 1442 to 1779.

facts.title: Keep your voice low in the hall
facts.text: People come here to worship.

facts.title: Cover shoulders and knees
facts.text: The usual advice for temples in Vietnam: dress modestly, with shoulders and knees covered, and take off your hat.

facts.title: Ask before photographing people
facts.text: Ask first, every time.

facts.title: Nearly a thousand years old
facts.text: Văn Miếu was built in 1070. Six years later, in 1076, a royal academy — Quốc Tử Giám — opened beside it.

facts.title: Khuê Văn Các
facts.text: This pavilion was built in 1805. Behind it lies Thiên Quang Tỉnh, a square pond.
